title: The VAE loss & architecture
blurb: Loss terms, BCE vs MSE, encoder/decoder networks

hook.title: Alice, Bob and the space mission
hook.text: Alice, in space, must send images to Bob on Earth. She compresses each image into a short **message** $\hat z$ (stochastically) and Bob decodes it. The scheme works if Bob's reconstruction is good, but there's a twist: if all messages are forced to follow a **standard shape** $p(z)$, then Bob — who knows that shape — can *invent plausible messages himself* and decode them into brand-new images, as if Alice had sent them.
hook.recall: Remember Alice and Bob: the reconstruction term makes messages decodable; the KL term forces them to a known standard shape so Bob can invent valid messages.

explore.intro: A toy 1-D VAE you can step through. The four boxes mirror the slide's procedure.
tasks: Step through 1→4 and watch each number appear. Which slider changes only $L_2$?
Try to drive both $L_1$ and $L_2$ to zero. What stops you?
explore.takeaway: Loss $\mathcal L=\alpha\mathcal L_1+\mathcal L_2$ with $\mathcal L_1=\|x-Dec(Enc(x))\|^2$ and $\mathcal L_2=D_{KL}[\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma)\|\mathcal N(0,1)]=-\tfrac12\sum(1+\log\sigma^2-\mu^2-\sigma^2)$.

questions.prompt: In the Alice–Bob story, why force messages to follow $p(z)$?
options: So Bob can generate realistic messages $\hat z\sim p(z)$ himself and decode them into images
questions.explanation: The KL term is what makes sampling from the prior legitimate.
$-\tfrac12(1+0-1-1)=0.5$. The mean sits one unit from the prior mean 0.

questions.prompt: Which reconstruction loss for which output assumption?
questions.explanation: Slide 28: assume Bernoulli use cross-entropy; assume Normal use MSE.

questions.prompt: Binary cross-entropy term from the slide: $-0.8\ln(0.9)$ (3 decimals).
questions.explanation: $-0.8\times(-0.10536)=0.0843$ (the slide shows 0.0842884). Compare $-0.8\ln0.7=0.2853$: a worse prediction costs more.

options: $\mathcal L_1$ is the reconstruction (squared error) loss
$\mathcal L_2$ is a KL term that keeps the latent space continuous and standard-normal
questions.explanation: The cross-entropy slide is titled “not symmetric”: $H(p,q)=-\sum p\log q$.

questions.prompt: The decoder ends in a softmax giving $D\times L$ categorical probabilities. A student trains with plain MSE on pixel values. What is the inconsistency?
options: With a Categorical $p_\theta(x|z)$ the reconstruction term is the categorical log-likelihood ($\ln\text{Categorical}(x|\theta(z))$), not MSE
MSE needs the softmax removed and the KL kept; no inconsistency
Softmax can’t be used in VAEs
questions.explanation: Slide 36: $p_\theta(x|z)=\text{Categorical}(x|\theta(z))$ gives the $\ln\text{Categorical}$ term in the ELBO.
